title: Lesson 6 · Relative & Interrogative Pronouns
blurb: Relative pronouns & clauses, antecedents, who/which/what, interrogatives, and pronoun mistakes.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“A man who is industrious will prosper.”
items.explain: “who” stands for “man” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“This is the house which my father bought.”
items.explain: “which” stands for “house” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“I gave him all that I had.”
items.explain: “that” stands for “all” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“I like a horse that is gentle.”
items.explain: “that” stands for “horse” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“Those who sow will reap.”
items.explain: “who” stands for “those” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“He will do what is right.”
items.explain: “what” means “that which” — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“The knife which you gave me is lost.”
items.explain: “which” stands for “knife” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the relative pronoun (it joins a clause to a noun)?

“The girl who sings is my sister.”
items.explain: “who” stands for “girl” and joins the clause — the relative pronoun.

items.prompt:
What is the antecedent (the word the relative stands for)?

“The boy who studies will learn.”
items.explain: “who” stands for “boy” — the antecedent.

items.prompt:
What is the antecedent (the word the relative stands for)?

“The fish which you caught is a trout.”
items.explain: “which” stands for “fish” — the antecedent.

items.prompt:
What is the antecedent (the word the relative stands for)?

“I like a horse that is gentle.”
items.explain: “that” stands for “horse” — the antecedent.

items.prompt:
What is the antecedent (the word the relative stands for)?

“Solomon, who was David’s son, built the temple.”
items.explain: “who” stands for “Solomon” — the antecedent.

items.prompt:
What is the antecedent (the word the relative stands for)?

“The knife which you gave me is lost.”
items.explain: “which” stands for “knife” — the antecedent.

items.prompt:
What is the antecedent (the word the relative stands for)?

“He is a man that deserves respect.”
items.explain: “that” stands for “man” — the antecedent.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank: who, which, or what?

“The girl ___ sings is my sister.”
items.explain: Use “who” for a person — the girl who sings.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank: who, which, or what?

“The book ___ fell was old.”
items.explain: Use “which” for a thing — the book which fell.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank: who, which, or what?

“He does ___ is right.”
items.explain: “what” means “that which” — he does what is right.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank: who, which, or what?

“The boy ___ studies will learn.”
items.explain: Use “who” for a person — the boy who studies.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank: who, which, or what?

“The ball ___ rolled away is lost.”
items.explain: Use “which” for a thing — the ball which rolled away.

items.prompt:
Fill the blank: who, which, or what?

“She has ___ she needs.”
items.explain: “what” means “that which” — she has what she needs.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interrogative pronoun (the question-word)?

“Who wrote that letter?”
items.explain: “Who” asks the question and stands alone — the interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interrogative pronoun (the question-word)?

“What did he say?”
items.explain: “What” asks the question and stands alone — the interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interrogative pronoun (the question-word)?

“Whom did you call?”
items.explain: “Whom” asks the question and stands alone — the interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the interrogative pronoun (the question-word)?

“Which is yours?”
items.explain: “Which” asks the question and stands alone — the interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Is the question-word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (before a noun)?

“Which comes first?”
items.explain: “Which” stands alone — an interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Is the question-word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (before a noun)?

“Which road shall I take?”
items.explain: “Which” comes before the noun “road” — an interrogative adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the question-word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (before a noun)?

“What noise is that?”
items.explain: “What” comes before the noun “noise” — an interrogative adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the question-word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (before a noun)?

“What can he mean?”
items.explain: “What” stands alone — an interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Is the question-word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (before a noun)?

“Whose book is this?”
items.explain: “Whose” comes before the noun “book” — an interrogative adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the question-word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (before a noun)?

“Who borrowed the slate?”
items.explain: “Who” stands alone — an interrogative pronoun.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“___ went in the boat.”
items.explain: Use subject forms and name yourself last: He and I went.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“It was ___.”
items.explain: After “was,” use the subject form: It was I.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“Is that book ___?”
items.explain: Possessive pronouns take no apostrophe: yours.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“No, it is ___.”
items.explain: Possessive pronouns take no apostrophe: hers.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“The victory is ___.”
items.explain: Possessive pronouns take no apostrophe: theirs.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“This house is ___.”
items.explain: Possessive pronouns take no apostrophe: ours.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“___ were tardy.”
items.explain: Name yourself last: He and I were tardy.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct form:

“___ were there.”
items.explain: Use the subject form and name yourself last: The doctor and I.
